cases.name: empty PATH entry is reported as the working directory
cases.stdin:
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho ran\n' > prog
chmod +x prog
PATH=":$PATH"

echo "[type]"
type prog; echo "rc=$?"
echo "[type -p]"
type -p prog; echo "rc=$?"
echo "[type -P]"
type -P prog; echo "rc=$?"
echo "[type -a]"
type -a prog; echo "rc=$?"
echo "[command -v]"
command -v prog; echo "rc=$?"

cases.name: empty PATH entry is reported the same wherever it appears
cases.stdin:
printf '#!/bin/sh\necho ran\n' > prog
chmod +x prog
original=$PATH

# Each of these keeps the rest of PATH reachable, so only the empty entry can
# account for finding `prog`, which exists solely in the working directory.
echo "[leading]"
PATH=":$original"; hash -r
command -v prog; echo "rc=$?"

echo "[trailing]"
PATH="$original:"; hash -r
command -v prog; echo "rc=$?"

echo "[middle]"
PATH="/nonexistent::$original"; hash -r
command -v prog; echo "rc=$?"

cases.name: $_ - exec does not override _ in child env
cases.stdin:
# bash does not set _ in the child's env for exec; the child inherits
# the parent's _ value. brush currently sets _ to the resolved command
# path (same as a normal external command), which is wrong for exec.
(exec $(which env)) | grep '^_='
